results.title: Behind Georges Larnicol's creative spin on Breton specialty kouign-amann
results.content: From a traditional Breton specialty to an imaginative, bite-sized creation, in Entre Nous we explore how French pastry chef Georges Larnicol has reinvented the famous kouign-amann while preserving its Breton identity. He tells us what makes the pastry so special and why it is much loved around the world.

results.title: UNICEF head Catherine Russell: 'We're all committed to the importance of children'
results.content: More than 50 countries, 20 non-governmental and philanthropic organisations and a series of multinational companies are pledging this week to put children's rights at the heart of their policies and actions. A pact is being agreed upon at the Paris Peace Forum, where the rights of children are taking centre stage.

results.title: Aneto, one of southern Europe's largest glaciers, is melting away
results.content: Within a decade, one of the largest glaciers in southern Europe will have disappeared. Aneto, the highest peak of the Spanish Pyrenees, is melting at a spectacular rate. Its demise is another sign of global warming and has much to teach glaciologists. FRANCE 24's Maude Petit-Jové, Mathilde Lopinski and Sarah Morris report.

results.title: 'France has some of the cleanest electricity in the world, but we're not using enough of it'
results.content: Eve Irvine is pleased to welcome Thierry Bros, energy & climate expert and Professor of Science and Economics at Sciences Po. As geopolitical conflicts unsettle global energy markets and governments struggle to reconcile climate commitments with economic and security imperatives, the answer lies in a fundamental reconsideration of the sequence of climate policy. "Electrification first," he argues, acknowledging that this "doesn't necessarily mean clean electricity." His argument is grounded in a critical assessment of international climate diplomacy and European energy policy. "We've seen many COPs, and they've all failed," he contends, questioning the effectiveness of ambitious targets that have yet to deliver the necessary structural transformation. results.title: 🔴Italy: At least 300 schools evacuated after email bomb alerts
Wave of hoax bomb threats sent to schools in UK, Ireland and Italy
results.content: Hundreds of schools in the UK, Italy and the Republic of Ireland received a "generic" threatening email on Wednesday now being treated as a hoax by authorities. Italy earlier evacuated roughly 300 schools over the perceived threat.

results.title: Pope Leo to end Argentina tour with outdoor mass before Peru 'homecoming'
results.content: Pope Leo will conclude his three-day visit to Argentina Wednesday with an outdoor mass expected to draw millions before continuing his tour of South America by travelling to Peru, where he once served as a missionary. The pontiff plans to deliver a speech in front of Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori, whose election earlier this year was marred ‌by fraud accusations and vote-counting delays.

results.title: Russia, Ukraine start second day of US-led talks: Kyiv lead negotiator
results.content: Russia and Ukraine have resumed US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi for a second day, Kyiv's chief negotiator Rustem Umerov said on Wednesday.

results.title: French journalist Christophe Gleizes marks 500 days in Algerian jail
results.content: Having been detained for 500 days in an Algerian prison on charges of “glorifying terrorism”, French journalist Christophe Gleizes continues to serve a seven-year sentence despite an intense campaign by his family and friends and the football world. While awaiting a presidential pardon, his supporters are stepping up their media campaign to secure his release. FRANCE 24 spoke with his friend Pierre de la Saussay.

results.title: Second day of Web Summit cancelled as Storm Charles puts Portugal on high alert
results.content: Portuguese authorities strongly advised organisers of the Web Summit to cancel events this Wednesday because of risks of tidal flooding and severe disruption to public transport. Storm Charles is expected to be at its most dangerous on Wednesday afternoon, with winds reaching up to 120 km/h and potentially very dangerous wind gusts as well.

results.title: Africa: Ghana waste dump poses health, environmental 'crisis'
results.content: An acrid haze hung over a sprawling dump in Ghana's capital, Accra, as excavators gouged into mounds of smouldering rubbish. Thin plumes of black smoke curled from burning plastic and rubber, mingling with the rank odour of stagnant lagoon water.
